procedural_history.originating_court: Not explicitly stated in the provided text, but it can be inferred that the case originated in a trial court within the State of Haryana, as the High Court of Punjab & Haryana was the first appellate court.
procedural_history.impugned_order: Judgment and Order dated 05.07.2023 of the High Court of Punjab & Haryana at Chandigarh in CRAD No. 224 of 2020
procedural_history.high_court_proceedings: The High Court of Punjab & Haryana at Chandigarh upheld the conviction of the appellants under Section 307 read with Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code and the sentence of 14 years rigorous imprisonment and a fine of Rs. 1,50,000 each.
procedural_history.supreme_court_posture: The appellants, Amit Rana @ Koka & Anr., filed a Special Leave Petition (converted to Criminal Appeal No. 700 of 2024) in the Supreme Court challenging their conviction and sentence. The Supreme Court initially declined to entertain the challenge to the conviction under Section 307 IPC, finding overwhelming evidence supporting it. The Court issued a limited notice confining the appeal to the challenge against the award of 14 years of rigorous imprisonment, specifically questioning whether a term of imprisonment beyond ten years is permissible under Section 307 IPC (except in cases of hurt during the attempt to murder).

directions: The imposition of rigorous imprisonment for 14 years each to the appellants is converted to rigorous imprisonment for a period of 10 years.
The order of sentence with respect to fine is kept intact.
The impugned judgment of the High Court and the judgment of the trial Court in S.T. No.281/2016 qua the appellants stands modified as above.

issue.issue_text: Whether a term of imprisonment beyond a period of ten years is permissible for an offence punishable under Section 307 Part 2, IPC (attempt to commit murder – causing hurt to any person), when the court chooses not to impose a sentence of imprisonment for life.

facts: The appellants were convicted for an offence under Section 307, Part 2 of the Indian Penal Code (IPC), which deals with an attempt to murder where hurt is caused.
The trial court, whose decision was confirmed by the High Court, sentenced the appellants to 14 years of rigorous imprisonment.
The Supreme Court's review was limited only to the question of whether this sentence was legally permissible, not the conviction itself.
The State had not filed an appeal seeking to enhance the punishment to life imprisonment.
law: The relevant law is Section 307 of the IPC, which the Court breaks down into parts.
Part 1 (attempt to murder simpliciter): Punishable with imprisonment for a term up to 10 years and a fine.
Part 2 (attempt to murder where hurt is caused): Punishable with "imprisonment for life, or to such punishment as is hereinbefore mentioned".
The Court's decision hinges on the interpretation of the phrase "or to such punishment as is hereinbefore mentioned" in Part 2.
application: The Supreme Court analyzed the structure of Section 307 and determined that for an offense under Part 2, the sentencing court has only two distinct options.
Option 1 is to impose a sentence of imprisonment for life.
Option 2, if life imprisonment is not chosen, is to impose "such punishment as is hereinbefore mentioned".

The Court reasoned that the phrase "hereinbefore mentioned" unambiguously refers back to the punishment prescribed in the first part of Section 307, which is imprisonment for a term that may not exceed 10 years.
Therefore, the Court concluded that the statute does not permit a sentence that falls between 10 years and life imprisonment.
Since the lower courts had decided against imposing a life sentence, the only legally available alternative was a punishment of up to 10 years.
reasoning.conclusion: The Supreme Court concluded that the imposition of a 14-year prison sentence for an offense under Section 307, Part 2, IPC is impermissible in law when the court has chosen not to impose a sentence of life imprisonment. The only other option available under the statute is a term that does not exceed 10 years.

arguments.issue_text: Whether a term of imprisonment beyond a period of ten years is permissible for an offence punishable under Section 307 Part 2, IPC (attempt to commit murder – causing hurt to any person), when the court chooses not to impose a sentence of imprisonment for life.
appellant_arguments: A term of imprisonment beyond ten years is impermissible under Section 307, IPC, when the court does not impose a sentence of imprisonment for life. The available punishments are either imprisonment for life or a term that cannot exceed ten years.
respondent_arguments: The respondent-State's argument, by implication of defending the lower courts' sentence, is that a term of imprisonment of 14 years is permissible under Section 307, IPC, as it is a lesser sentence than the maximum punishment of life imprisonment.

ratio_decidendi.ratio: When a court convicts an individual under Section 307 of the Indian Penal Code and opts not to impose a sentence of life imprisonment, the maximum permissible term of imprisonment that can be awarded is 10 years.
obiter: The offence to commit murder punishable under Section 307, IPC is constituted by the concurrence of mens rea followed by actus reus, to commit an attempt to murder though its accomplishment or sufferance of any kind of bodily injury to the victim is not a ‘sine qua non’.
Section 307, IPC imbibes the true spirit of the maxim ‘culpae poena per esto’ meaning ‘let the punishment be proportioned to the crime’.

judicial_reasoning.core_finding: For an offence under the second part of Section 307, IPC, where hurt is caused, the court has only two sentencing options: imprisonment for life, or the punishment prescribed in the first part of the section, which is imprisonment for a term not exceeding 10 years. A term of imprisonment that is more than 10 years but less than life, such as the 14-year sentence imposed by the lower courts, is impermissible in law.
legal_tests_applied: Statutory Interpretation of Section 307, IPC: The court analyzed the provision by dividing it into two parts. The first part deals with an attempt to murder where no hurt is caused, carrying a maximum sentence of 10 years. The second part deals with an attempt to murder where hurt is caused, for which the offender is liable 'either to imprisonment for life, or to such punishment as is hereinbefore mentioned.' The court interpreted 'hereinbefore mentioned' as a direct reference to the punishment specified in the first part of the section.
